new_statements.rule_in_words: No source states anything about word stress in Jalaa. The only open statement is Blench's second-hand inference from Kleinewillinghöfer's 2001 wordlist transcriptions that Jalaa is a tone language with three level tones plus a falling tone; the wordlist forms (Wiktionary copy) carry grave/acute/circumflex tone marks and no stress marks. Stress is simply unaddressed.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Blench notes vowel length is transcribed on some words (yúú 'sesame') but that its systematicity cannot be determined.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms from a wordlist (Kleinewillinghöfer 2001: 264-270 per Wiktionary); no phrasal or grammatical data exist. Blench's statement is an inference from another author's transcriptions, not a first-hand description.
new_statements.identity_note: Jalaa = Centúúm/Cèntûm/Cuŋ Tuum = Jaa (Glottolog cent2045, ISO cet), an isolate remembered by a few elders of the Jalaabe at Loojaa, who now speak the Bwilim dialect of Cham/Dikaka (dika1234? not verified) — Blench 2011 Atlas entry '67. Cen Tuum'. All sources describe the same single variety; the language is probably extinct (last rememberers in their eighties per the Mainz Tula-Waja page).
